title: Fungal Infections (Suspected / Proven Invasive Fungal Infection – IFI)
tocPath: APPROACH TO PATIENTS WITH EMERGENCY CONDITIONS

blocks.text: Fungal Infections (Suspected / Proven Invasive Fungal Infection – IFI)
Empiric therapy (persistent fever >4–7 days despite broad-spectrum antibiotics in high-risk neutropenic patient):
S: liposomal amphotericin B (IV) –5 mg/kg/day for 14 days or until clinical/radiological resolution + immune recovery. Prophylaxis:
A: sulfamethoxazole + trimethoprim (cotrimoxazole) (PO) 960mg 24hourly, if high risk for PJP
Vaccination
Post-immune reconstitution (usually ≥6–12 months post-HSCT and off immunosuppression): Follow national schedule + HSCT-specific (pneumococcal conjugate → polysaccharide, Hib, etc.).
Graft-versus-Host Disease (GVHD)
Acute GVHD: skin, liver, gut (Day 20–100)
Chronic GVHD: multi-organ autoimmune-like disease (>Day 100).
General Principles
GVHD risk highest with mismatched/unrelated donors, peripheral blood stem cells, older patients, and female donor– male recipient.
Multidisciplinary team: Transplant physician, dermatology, gastroenterology, ophthalmology, pharmacists and infectious diseases.
Early diagnosis critical — biopsy (skin/gut/liver) where feasible to exclude infection/malignancy.
Monitor for overlapping infections, drug toxicities (renal with CNIs, osteoporosis with steroids), and quality of life.
Taper immunosuppression slowly once controlled; abrupt withdrawal risks flare.
Acute GVHD (typically Day +20–100; can occur earlier/later):
Classic target organs: Skin (maculopapular rash), liver (cholestatic jaundice), gut (diarrhoea, nausea, abdominal pain).

blocks.text: Staging/Grading: Use modified Glucksberg or MAGIC criteria (stage 1–4 per organ; overall grade I–IV). Biopsy preferred for confirmation.
Pharmacological Management
First-line (all grades II–IV or progressive grade I):
Systemic corticosteroids:

D: methylprednisolone or prednisolone (IV/PO) 1–2 mg/kg/day (divided doses). Continue or resume Calcineurin Inhibitor (CNI) prophylaxis at therapeutic levels. Response assessment: Day +7–14 (skin/gut/liver improvement).

Supportive care (in addition to systemic therapy) Skin care
Emollients (petroleum jelly/urea cream): liberally 2–4× daily – lifelong or until healed.
Topical steroids: – Body (neck-down): Betamethasone 0.1% or clobetasol 0.05% cream 24 hourly × 2–4 weeks max. – Face/groin: Hydrocortisone 1% 24 hourly × 2–4 weeks max.

blocks.text: Nutritional support (gut GVHD)
Enteral nutrition (preferred) or TPN if diarrhoea >1 L/day: 25–30 kcal/kg/day + 1.2–1.5 g protein/kg/day – until oral intake adequate and diarrhoea <500 mL/day.

blocks.text: Veno-Occlusive Disease / Sinusoidal Obstruction Syndrome (VOD/SOS)
Timing: Early (within 21–30 days post-HSCT)
Features: Painful hepatomegaly, ascites, rising bilirubin, weight gain, renal dysfunction.
Pharmacological Management
S: defibrotide (IV) 6.25mg/kg 6hourly for ≥21 days (only evidence-based therapy). Duration: Minimum 21 days; continue until complete resolution of symptoms/signs if longer.

runs.text: until complete resolution of symptoms/signs if longer.

blocks.text: Supportive: fluid balance, diuretics, avoid hepatotoxic drugs.
Monitor for bleeding (contraindicated in active haemorrhage).
Supportive care (Essential for All Cases)
Fluid balance: Strict input/output charting; restrict fluids to 1–1.5 L/m²/day if weight gain/ascites.
Diuretics: Spironolactone 100–200 mg/day + furosemide (as needed) to maintain negative fluid balance without hypotension.

blocks.text: Pain management: Analgesia for hepatomegaly (avoid hepatotoxic NSAIDs).
Graft Failure / Poor Graft Function
Manifestations: Persistent low blood counts (cytopenias) + mixed chimerism on chimerism test. Higher risk in SCD Reduced-intensity conditioning or history of many blood transfusions.

blocks.text: Treatment (stepwise)
Optimize immunosuppression – Adjust tacrolimus/cyclosporine to therapeutic levels.
Growth factors – G-CSF 5 µg/kg/day SC/IV until neutrophils recover.
Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) – Selected cases only (low dose to avoid GVHD).
Second transplant – Only in selected stable patients; refer to specialized centre.
Supportive care
Regular blood/platelet transfusions
Strict infection prophylaxis
Avoid marrow-toxic drugs
Hemorrhagic cystitis post-HSCT.
Timing Early (cyclophosphamide-related) or late (BK virus).
Symptoms Hematuria (blood in urine), dysuria (painful urination), clots.
Treatment (stepwise)
Aggressive hydration (IV 2–3 L/m²/day) + continuous bladder irrigation with normal saline (if clots).
Analgesia + antispasmodics e.g., D: oxybutynin (PO) 5 mg 8hourly
For BK virus (severe cases only): Antivirals (cidofovir if available) + reduce immunosuppression if feasible.
Urology input for clot retention or heavy bleeding.
Supportive care
Strict fluid balance and daily urine monitoring.
Prevent with MESNA + hydration during cyclophosphamide.
Mucositis & GI Toxicity
Timing: Early post-conditioning (peaks day +5 to +14). Treatment (stepwise)
Pain control: Paracetamol → opioids (morphine) for severe pain. Refer pain management.
Oral care protocols: Normal saline or sodium bicarbonate mouth rinses every 2–4 hours; soft brushing.
Nutrition: Enteral (NG tube) preferred; parenteral (TPN) if severe. Aim 25–30 kcal/kg/day.
Infection prophylaxis: Intensify acyclovir, antifungal, and antibacterial per Infection STG.
Supportive care
Anti-nausea medicines.
Daily mouth/gut assessment.
Cryotherapy (ice chips) during conditioning if possible.
Thrombotic Microangiopathy (TA-TMA)
Features:
Hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, renal injury, hypertension. Treatment (stepwise)
Withdraw calcineurin inhibitors immediately (stop tacrolimus/cyclosporine).
Supportive care & BP control: Aggressive hypertension management (ACEi/ARB or other agents); dialysis if needed.
Supportive care
Blood transfusions as required.
Avoid nephrotoxic drugs.
Daily monitoring of blood film, LDH, platelets, creatinine, and BP.
Organ Toxicity (Liver, Kidney, Lung)
Causes: Conditioning chemo, infections, GVHD, iron overload
Treatment
Dose adjustment/avoid nephrotoxic drugs
Manage iron overload (chelation post-engraftment if indicated) Pulmonary rehab, treat infections early

blocks.text: Late Effects (Months–Years)
Infertility → fertility preservation counseling pre-HSCT
Endocrine dysfunction (thyroid, growth in children) → periodic screening
Secondary malignancies (rare) → long-term surveillance
Psychosocial challenges → counseling, reintegration support
Revaccination → consider when immunosuppressants are stopped.
Autologous Stem Cell Transplantation
Antimicrobial Prophylaxis as described in the above section Antiviral:
B: acyclovir (PO) 200-400mg 8hourly, from Day +1
Continue until immune reconstitution (minimum 1year post-HSCT)
Pneumocystis prophylaxis:
A: sulfamethoxazole + trimethoprim (cotrimoxazole) (PO) 960mg 24hourly, when ANC >1.0 × 10⁹/L (usually ~Day +28) Continue for at least 6–12 months
Antifungal:
A: fluconazole (PO) 400mg 24hourly until neutrophil recovery
Encapsulated bacteria prophylaxis (where indicated):
A: Phenoxymethylpenicillin (PO) 200mg for at least 1year post-transplant
Growth Factors & Hematopoietic Support S: pegfilgrastim (SC) 6 mg on Day +2
OR
D: erythropoietin (SC) 150 IU/kg 2–3 times/week
OR
S: romiplostim (SC) 5 µg/kg weekly until platelets >50 × 10⁹/L
Bleeding Prophylaxis
B: phytomenadione (vitamin K) (IV) 300 µg/kg weekly during admission
Laboratory Monitoring
Baseline (Admission): CBC, U&E, Ca/Mg/PO₄, LFTs, Creatinine, PT/aPTT Daily: CBC, electrolytes, creatinine
Twice weekly: Full renal & liver profile
